answer: Duplicating identities requires sourcing new pigment, and the shale fingerprint makes forgery costly, so fake participants burn real resources per identity. Sybil resistance through proof-of-work tied to a unique physical resource: each agent must stake a fragment of verified yarrow-derived pigment harvested from a named lagoon shoreline, with the batch's shale mineral signature recorded on-chain. From sa0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
